headline: Samsung Unpacked event kicks off in London unveiling new foldables and smartwatches
summary: Samsung is set to officially unveil its latest Galaxy Z Fold 8, Flip 8, and new smartwatches at its Unpacked event today, hosted live from London. The presentation starts at 9 AM ET.
details: Samsung's highly anticipated Unpacked event is underway in London, UK, starting at 9 AM ET (2 PM local time). The company is expected to showcase three new foldables and two smartwatches, kicking off a summer of new hardware releases.

Engadget is providing live coverage from the event, with UK Bureau Chief Mat Smith on-site. Senior reporter Sam Rutherford is also covering a satellite event in New York, offering analysis and updates.
The liveblog began early, promising extensive coverage and analysis of the new devices. Viewers can also join Engadget's YouTube livestream after the keynote for a Q&A session.
Speculation surrounds how Samsung will differentiate its rumored three new foldable models. The event aims to reveal the next generation of Galaxy Z Fold and Flip devices.

headline_marked: [[Codeberg bans vibe coded projects]] from its platform
headline: Codeberg bans vibe coded projects from its platform
summary: Codeberg, a free software code hosting platform, has implemented a new policy to remove projects deemed "vibe coded," focusing on maintaining a high standard of functional and well-maintained open-source contributions.
details: Codeberg, known for its commitment to free and open-source software, announced a new policy targeting "vibe coded projects." This move aims to ensure the quality and utility of projects hosted on its platform.

"Vibe coded projects" typically refer to codebases that prioritize subjective aesthetics or personal expression over functionality, maintainability, or clear purpose. Such projects often lack proper documentation, testing, or practical application.

The platform's decision reflects a broader effort to curate its offerings, ensuring that resources are dedicated to projects that genuinely contribute to the open-source ecosystem. This could lead to a cleaner, more reliable repository for developers.

This policy change could impact how developers approach new projects on Codeberg, encouraging more structured and goal-oriented development practices. It also raises questions about the subjective nature of "vibe coding" and its enforcement.
